newsitem.title: JAPAN: Suzutan president to be replaced by son in March.
newsitem.headline: Suzutan president to be replaced by son in March.

text.p: Japanese retailer Suzutan Co Ltd said on Wednesday that its president, Katsurao Suzui, would step down on March 1, 1997 and be replaced by his son, executive managing director Shunji Suzui.
The elder Suzui, who will become an adviser to the company, is currently the target of a probe by the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission into alleged insider trading.
A company spokesman said the reshuffle was in line with Katsurao Suzui's intention to resign from the president's post after a two-year term.

The spokesman added that the president's decision to step down was motivated in part by a desire to take responsibility for the insider trading scandal, although he had not admitted guilt in the case.

The elder Suzui earlier acknowledged that he sold 1.01 million shares in the company prior to an announcement of a loss for the 1994/95 business year, but said he did not regard this as improper insider trading.
The Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission declined to comment on whether or not the probe had ended.
